articleTitle: Medical Image Encryption for Advanced Security and Privacy
publicationTitle: 2024 Second International Conference on Smart Technologies for Power and Renewable Energy (SPECon)
abstract: Through its cutting-edge methods of remote diagnosis and quicker first aid delivery, telemedicine and numerous telemedicinal applications are transforming a range of healthcare departments. In these applications, the use of digital images is crucial for assuring better and quicker health outcomes. These digital photographs are typically transferred between hospitals, doctors, and patients through open networks, often containing private and diagnostic data about the patients. To ensure the patient’s privacy, it is necessary to safeguard them while they are being stored and transported.This study presents a chaotic image encryption system that makes use of two chaotic maps, namely Arnold Cat Map and 2D-LSCM, to increase the randomness and security of the encrypted image. We contrast our method with other well-known chaotic picture encryption systems and examine the effectiveness and security of our scheme.

articleTitle: Meta-Heuristic Algorithm Based Asymmetric Multilevel Inverter for Addressing Power Quality Issues
publicationTitle: 2024 Second International Conference on Smart Technologies for Power and Renewable Energy (SPECon)
abstract: In power electronics, multilevel inverters are essential for increasing power quality, boosting efficiency, and lowering harmonic distortion. This paper presents a new method for generating pulse patterns in multilevel inverters by using the Northern Goshawk Optimization Algorithm (NGOA). The 125-level Asymmetric Multi-Level Inverter is designed and employed to address power quality concerns like sag and swell. The Northern Goshawk Optimization Algorithm is utilized to develop pulse patterns in multilevel inverter systems with the goal of attaining enhanced performance, drawing inspiration from the hunting techniques of goshawks. The primary device in the Custom power devices, the DSTATCOM, utilizes power electronic elements to control power flow and improve power quality in power grids. This study aims to uphold voltage stability within the power system by fine-tuning reactive power through the design and application of a DSTATCOM (Distributed Static Synchronous Compensator) based on a 125- level Asymmetric Multi-Level Inverter, employing the Goshawk Optimization Algorithm.

articleTitle: Analysis of a bidirectional converter for electric vehicles using photovoltaic panels
publicationTitle: 2024 Second International Conference on Smart Technologies for Power and Renewable Energy (SPECon)
abstract: This study presents an analysis of the bidirectional converter for electric vehicle charging that is based on solar panels. A photovoltaic cell battery and a bidirectional converter that converts DC to DC make up this system. A battery is included to ensure the DC (direct current) engine can run when there isn’t enough sunshine. Excess energy from the photovoltaic (PV) panel may be stored in the battery since the bidirectional dc-de converter may control the flow of energy in both directions while it charges and discharges the battery. The MPPT controller takes the greatest power out of the photovoltaic module as load and irradiance changes. The model’s output was assessed and analysed using MATLAB/Simulink.

articleTitle: A Simulation based driven method to Optimize the efficiency of long Transmission lines using Photo Voltaic Power Generation Technique
publicationTitle: 2024 Second International Conference on Smart Technologies for Power and Renewable Energy (SPECon)
abstract: This research explores the application of renewable resources, specifically photovoltaic power generation, for efficient long-distance transmission. We are motivated by the pressing need for improved energy transmission in regions like Pakistan and other Asian countries, where abundant oil resources are minimum. These areas currently face significant greenhouse gas emissions from their energy sectors, contributing to rising temperatures. Coal, a carbon-based fossil fuel, dominates the energy production landscape, comprising one-third of total capacity. To address these challenges, we have integrated photovoltaic systems with Ultra-Lift Luo (ULL) Converters to enhance transmission efficiency. DC-DC converters commonly suffer from energy losses, especially due to switching losses during hard switching, significantly diminishing overall system efficiency, To overcome this, we have implemented the Zero Voltage Switching (ZVS) Scheme, ensuring precise device activation near zero crossings, thereby adopting a softer switching approach that substantially improves system efficiency. Following this enhancement, an inverter transforms these stepped-up voltages into AC voltage, which is subsequently transmitted through underground cables to a transformer for distribution. Our research also includes sensitivity analysis, wherein we vary the PV capacity to assess its impact on overall system performance. These experiments have been meticulously simulated using MATLAB/Simulink. Our study aims to optimize the power transmission process, offering promising benefits for the energy landscape in Pakistan and similar regions, thereby promoting sustainable energy solutions.

articleTitle: Impact of Large Scale Renewable Energy Integration on the Grid Frequency
publicationTitle: 2024 Second International Conference on Smart Technologies for Power and Renewable Energy (SPECon)
abstract: The conventional power system is subjected to more frequency stability issues like generation loss, increased steady state frequency deviation, cascading failures, and frequent operation of frequency relays due to integration of renewable power into the grid. Integrating renewable power such as wind and solar, cause reduction in system inertia. This impact is reflected on the frequency indices such as rate of change of frequency, frequency nadir, and settling frequency. The frequency indices of the IEEE 57 bus system with 7 thermal generators is compared with the frequency indices of IEEE 57 bus with 5 thermal generators and 2 wind generators and also with the frequency indices of the IEEE 57 bus with 5 thermal generators and 2 solar photovoltaic. The results proves that, as renewable power is integrated, the rate of change of frequency and frequency nadir get increased, and the settling frequency is decreased. The study concludes that, as the renewable integration is increased the system inertia is decreased. MATPOWER and MATLAB SIMULINK is used for simulation.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of Microcontroller based Smart Battery Management System
publicationTitle: 2024 Second International Conference on Smart Technologies for Power and Renewable Energy (SPECon)
abstract: Electric vehicles are gaining popularity in India as a significant new trend in the automobile industry. These vehicles play a crucial role in protecting our world from air pollution. Batteries are used by them to store the energy needed to run. To keep these batteries in top shape, an efficient battery management system (BMS) is required. This article describes a smart BMS that can be utilized in any device equipped with lithium-ion battery banks. The system includes a device for tracking, measuring, and diagnosing lithium-ion battery efficiency and conservation. Among the hardware and software components of the BMS architecture are sensors, the ESP8266 microcontroller, and a cloud system. Together with an ACS71230A current sensor module that can measure currents up to 30A, the ESP8266 functions as the BMS controller and CPU. Additionally, a DS18B20 module is employed to monitor temperature, while a voltage sensor measures battery voltage. To accommodate the voltage sensor’s rating, a buck converter is installed between the voltage sensor and the battery.

articleTitle: Efficient Single-Phase 15-Level Inverter Design for Enhanced Solar PV Integration
publicationTitle: 2024 Second International Conference on Smart Technologies for Power and Renewable Energy (SPECon)
abstract: This paper presents an efficient design and implementation of a single-phase 15-level inverter tailored for solar photovoltaic (PV) applications, leveraging MATLAB/Simulink for simulation and analysis. The proposed inverter architecture achieves an elevated level of performance through advanced control strategies and reduced component count. The integration of solar PV systems demands inverters that offer improved power quality, reliability, and energy harvesting. Our design addresses these requirements by employing a sophisticated control algorithm to optimize voltage levels while significantly reducing the number of components, enhancing overall system efficiency and reliability. The MATLAB/Simulink platform is utilized for comprehensive simulation, providing valuable insights into the inverter’s behaviour under varying operating conditions. The results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed design in terms of output waveform quality, reduced losses, and enhanced energy extraction from solar PV sources, validating its suitability for real-world solar power applications. This research paper contributes to the ongoing efforts to enhance the efficiency and reliability of renewable energy systems, particularly in the context of solar PV integration.

articleTitle: Enhanced Short-Term Photovoltaic Power Prediction using a Hybrid Improved Whale Optimization Algorithm with XGBoost
publicationTitle: 2024 Second International Conference on Smart Technologies for Power and Renewable Energy (SPECon)
abstract: Grid-connected photovoltaic (PV) systems are becoming more and more popular in the renewable energy space, but their volatility and unpredictability present difficulties, especially in the event of variable weather. In order to address these issues, accurate PV power forecasting becomes essential for efficient grid management. In order to address this, we present a model called IMWOA-XGB, which combines XGBoost and the Improved Whale Optimization Algorithm (IMWOA). With the help of our model, PV power projections should be more accurate, allowing for the creation of well-informed generation plans that reduce the grid effect of PV systems. The root mean square error (RMSE) is 18.867 and the mean absolute error (MAE) is 8.639 for the suggested model.

articleTitle: Study for Reliability of Quasi Z Source Inverter in stand alone PV system with battery
publicationTitle: 2024 Second International Conference on Smart Technologies for Power and Renewable Energy (SPECon)
abstract: A standalone PV system is a better alternative in remote and places of frequent power failure. In order to practically implement a standalone PV system, performance analysis and reliability analysis of the system is important. In this paper reliability analysis for Quasi Z Source Inverter with a battery is compared with the existing topologies of stand-alone PV system. The existing topologies are DC SEPIC converter and DC boost converter. The charging and discharging of the battery is controlled by a bidirectional DC converter. A 3 KW single phase system is designed and implemented in MATLAB Simulink. The reliability of the entire system is assessed by Reliability Block Diagram method. Mean Time Between Failure of the entire system is derived and results are plotted for Quasi Z Source inverter, DC SEPIC converter and DC Boost converter considered with battery. Comparative reliability plot of the considered systems is shown for a time period of six years. The Total Harmonic Distortion of output voltage and the magnitude of output voltage for the cases considered is maintained within the standard limits.

articleTitle: Active Switched Inductor Capacitor Based Boost Converter For DC Motor Load
publicationTitle: 2024 Second International Conference on Smart Technologies for Power and Renewable Energy (SPECon)
abstract: Based on the high step-up DC DC converter using active switched LC network for photovoltaic systems, This paper outlines the functionality of a boost converter using the principle of active switched inductor capacitor for DC motor load. The structure is simple and gives high voltage gain. Simulation studies are done on MATLAB tool to validate the converter..

articleTitle: Novel Hybrid Approach for Advancing Power System Security Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 Second International Conference on Smart Technologies for Power and Renewable Energy (SPECon)
abstract: The persistent recurrence of power system blackouts in recent years underscores the pressing need to address voltage instability and its subsequent collapse. This study proposes a novel solution in the form of the Hybrid Line Stability Ranking Index (HLSRI), tailored specifically for forecasting voltage collapse within power system networks (PSNs). Using a thorough development process, HLSRI combines the basic expressions of the Line Stability Index (Lmn) and the Fast Voltage Stability Index (FVSI). It also includes a switching logic based on voltage angle differentials, which are known to happen before voltage collapse. Testing HLSRI on the IEEE 30-bus system shows that it works, as it gives results that are similar to known indicators in both normal and emergencies. Notably, under contingency analysis, the vulnerability of bus 30 emerges, with the line connecting bus 06 to bus 10 identified as critical. However, HLSRI, alongside Lmn and FVSI, exhibits consistent values, affirming its accuracy in gauging line stability amidst system perturbations. The research underscores the importance of innovative methodologies like HLSRI in fortifying power system resilience against disruptive events, thus advancing the field of power system stability analysis.

articleTitle: Fast Optimization Algorithm for Switched Mode Power Supplies: Minimal Data-Sheet-Driven Algorithms Enhancing Active and Passive Component Performance
publicationTitle: 2024 Second International Conference on Smart Technologies for Power and Renewable Energy (SPECon)
abstract: This paper introduces a new tool for the optimization of switched mode power supplies suitable for both inexperienced and experienced design engineers. Employing sophisticated algorithms with minimal data sheet inputs, this framework achieves notable enhancements for magnetic components, electrolytic capacitors, switching components (MOSFET, IGBT, and extensible to SiC and GaN components). This tool is designed to be user-friendly, making it accessible for those with limited experience while still offering advanced capabilities for seasoned engineers. This intelligent approach ensures efficient utilization of resources, offering significant advancements in power supply design with reduced reliance on extensive data sheet information.

articleTitle: Integrated Tool for Cleaning Bulk Solar Power Data
publicationTitle: 2024 Second International Conference on Smart Technologies for Power and Renewable Energy (SPECon)
abstract: Cleaning of photovoltaic (PV) power generation data is an important step during data pre-processing stage in a data analytics program. Scope of solar PV generation data analysis include solar power generation forecasting, energy management, optimal design of solar plants etc. Machine Learning applications in power sector are emerging rapidly in recent years. The intermittent nature of the output power of PV systems makes it difficult for a data engineer to pre-process the erroneous solar PV generation data. The proposed data cleansing algorithm aims to help the data engineer without domain expertise to process exclusive solar PV generation data. Generalized data cleansing tools like R and Python, holds many inbuilt tools to clean bulk data set. A machine learning based approach have been proposed to replace the missing values of the solar power and energy data set, with more suitable values, thereby minimizing the intervention of a solar data expert. Finally, the performance analysis of the developed algorithm is carried out using bulk solar power data collected from a roof top solar plant.

articleTitle: Home Energy Management System in Kerala by using Advanced Metering Infrastructure
publicationTitle: 2024 Second International Conference on Smart Technologies for Power and Renewable Energy (SPECon)
abstract: The modern world faces pressing challenges in sustainable energy management and consumption. In response to the increasing demand for electricity and the necessity for efficient energy utilization, the development of smart metering systems coupled with advanced technologies has emerged as a pivotal solution. This paper explores the conception, design, and implementation of a smart energy metering system equipped with innovative features, aiming to revolutionize conventional energy monitoring and management methodologies. With a core emphasis on integrating machine learning, IoT technologies, and demand-side management, this endeavor seeks to not only enhance real-time energy monitoring capabilities but also empower users to make informed decisions about their energy usage patterns. This paper delves into the detailed architecture, methodologies, challenges, and potential socio-economic impacts of deploying such a smart energy metering system.

articleTitle: Boost Converter Powered by Thermoelectric Generator to Harvest Low Temperature Waste Heat
publicationTitle: 2024 Second International Conference on Smart Technologies for Power and Renewable Energy (SPECon)
abstract: This article discusses a self-starting low voltage low input impedance dc-dc boost converter that powers electronic devices by gathering body heat using a thermoelectric generator (TEG). TEGs with low input impedance can produce moderate power but the output voltage (a few mV) is low. Such TEG operating at low temperatures needs a boost converter to directly power any electronic devices. In this study, a common drain amplifier with transformer feedback is employed to demonstrate a frequency-independent high gain. Its low voltage self-starting capability enables the boost converter to start at the lowest input voltage. The flyback converter as a boost converter offers a low input impedance which makes the converter circuit suitable for TEG applications. The simple supervisory IC based logic circuit connects or disconnects the load according to the requirement. The boost converter consumes $41 \mu \mathrm{W}$ power to self-starts at 16mV. It achieves $72 \%$ maximum efficiency at an input voltage of 59mV. The output voltage of $2.72 \mathrm{~V}$ and power of $4.47 \mathrm{~mW}$ at maximum efficiency are sufficient for low-power electrical gadgets.

articleTitle: Modified SoC Based Droop Control for A Standalone DC Nanogrid
publicationTitle: 2024 Second International Conference on Smart Technologies for Power and Renewable Energy (SPECon)
abstract: A modified state-of-charge (SoC) based power management technique for a DC nanogrid is presented in this paper. A DC nanogrid consists of a rooftop Photovoltaic source, battery systems, and various DC loads connected to it. Although the majority of current methods depend on communication links to achieve the intended results, this power management technique uses the DC bus signaling method, in which the DC bus voltage serves as an information carrier. The life of the battery is adversely affected if it is discharged below its minimum SoC level or if it charges more than the maximum SoC level. So, a Power flow algorithm based on the SoC of the battery is developed and also level of charging and discharging currents is also considered to avoid overcharging and over-discharging of batteries. To analyze the effectiveness the same is simulated in MATLAB/Simulink

articleTitle: Improved Droop Control Algorithm for Accurate Load Sharing and Circulating Current Minimization in a Low-Voltage DC Grid
publicationTitle: 2024 Second International Conference on Smart Technologies for Power and Renewable Energy (SPECon)
abstract: The dc microgrid consists of several dc-dc converters connected together, operating in parallel and requires accurate control for its smooth operation. Maintaining accurate current sharing between the parallel connected converters in the grid is a challenging issue. The voltage regulation at the grid should also be maintained within permissible limits. Droop control method is one of the most widely used techniques for power flow control in parallel connected systems. However, the main demerit of conventional droop control is that it suffers from a compromise between current sharing accuracy and voltage regulation requirements. Any mismatch in the individual converter output voltages results in circulating currents between the converters which increases the losses and reduces the efficiency. This paper proposes an improved droop control method for accurate load sharing among parallel connected dc-dc converters and it limits the circulating current also. The control algorithm and detailed analysis is explained for two parallel connected boost converters. The effectiveness of the proposed droop control method is verified with the help of simulations done in MATLAB Simulink.

articleTitle: Solar Power Optimizer Design and MPPT Control using Flyback Converter
publicationTitle: 2024 Second International Conference on Smart Technologies for Power and Renewable Energy (SPECon)
abstract: This paper presents a solar power optimizer (SPO) system to efficiently harvest the maximum amount of energy from each PV panel and integrate it with a DC bus. The proposed SPO employs a flyback converter, which operates with the P&O maximum power point tracking algorithm. The efficacy of these SPO systems is significantly improved, particularly under partial shading conditions, where centralized PV systems incur substantial losses. The performance of the 1 kW SPO system is evaluated in the presence of two different partial shading patterns and compared with the results of the centralized converter system. Simulation results show that the proposed SPO system has a tracking efficiency above 99.5 %, enhancing the overall performance and making it a potentially viable solution for PV applications.

articleTitle: A Frequency Regulation of an Isolated Distributed Generation with Electric Vehicle and Battery Management System Integration Using Artificial Neural Network Technique
publicationTitle: 2024 Second International Conference on Smart Technologies for Power and Renewable Energy (SPECon)
abstract: The rising mix of environmentally friendly power sources in dispersed age frameworks requires hearty recurrence guideline systems to keep up with lattice solidity. This paper presents a clever way to address this test by coordinating Electric Vehicles (EVs) and Battery Management Systems (BMS) into a separate, disseminated age framework. The center of the proposed framework lies in the use of Artificial Neural Networks (ANN) for continuous dynamics in recurrence guidelines. The framework parts incorporate sustainable sources, a circulated age unit, energy capacity as batteries, and electric vehicles. The MATLAB/Simulink stage is utilized for the demonstration and reproduction of the whole framework. The battery-board framework guarantees proficient charging and releasing of batteries, while electric vehicles add to the general framework elements. An Artificial Neural Network (ANN) is used to foresee and control recurrence deviations. The brain network is prepared utilizing a data set produced from different working circumstances. Input highlights to the brain network incorporate power yields from sustainable sources, battery State of Charge (SOC), and other pertinent boundaries, with the result being the recurrence deviation. Recreation results exhibit the viability of the proposed framework in keeping up with recurrence security under shifting circumstances. The mix of EVs and BMS, combined with the prescient capacities of the brain organization, adds to further development of constant recurrence guideline in separated, dispersed age frameworks. The introduced approach gives a promising answer for improving the dependability and execution of future environmentally friendly power frameworks.

articleTitle: Analysis of Perturb & Observe MPPT Algorithm in Partial Shading for DC-DC Boost Converters
publicationTitle: 2024 Second International Conference on Smart Technologies for Power and Renewable Energy (SPECon)
abstract: It introduces an enhanced MPPT algorithm for addressing Partial Shading Conditions (PSC) affecting solar panels integrated with a DC-DC converter. The Perturb and Observe (P&O) technique is employed by the suggested methodology to control and normalize the non-linear output of PV systems operating under PSC. Unlike the conventional Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) method, which exhibited limited effectiveness in PSC scenarios, the P&O method demonstrates the ability to effectively manage both global and local peaks, leading to enhanced operational efficiency. PSO fails to adapt to PSC due to its inability to handle varying power flows efficiently, resulting in constant power output with decreased efficiency. The comparative analysis validates the proposed approach mathematically, with results extensively discussed. The proposed topology is modelled using MATLAB/Simulink software to substantiate its advantages

articleTitle: State of Health Estimation for Second Life Lithium-Ion Batteries: Indicators and Considerations
publicationTitle: 2024 Second International Conference on Smart Technologies for Power and Renewable Energy (SPECon)
abstract: This study aims to provide valuable insights into state of health estimation of second-life lithium-ion batteries in stationary energy storage systems by conducting an analytical examination of key technical indicators and considerations. By considering these factors, we can enhance our understanding of the estimation process and make informed decisions regarding the conditions of utilizing these batteries in their second life. The approach, presented in this paper, focuses on two main aspects. Firstly, it takes into account the unique characteristics of these batteries, which exhibit different responses to operational factors compared to their initial life cycle in electrical vehicles. Secondly, it considers monitoring conditions of stationary storage systems to develop an enhanced monitoring system which leads to an efficient performance of batteries in their second-life. By addressing these aspects, we aim to optimize the utilization of second-life batteries in stationary storage systems and ensure their reliable operation. This methodology, which utilizes Kalman filter and empirically derived data, has demonstrated significantly improved reliability and accuracy compared to other methodologies. By leveraging Kalman filter, we were able to enhance the estimation process and achieve a more precise estimation of state of health in stationary energy storage systems.

articleTitle: Marine Inspection: Implementation and Advanced Applications of a Remotely Operated Underwater Robot for Exploration in Challenging Marine Environments
publicationTitle: 2024 Second International Conference on Smart Technologies for Power and Renewable Energy (SPECon)
abstract: Robots that operate underwater that are remotely operated (ROVs) have become indispensable for a wide range of underwater tasks, from environmental monitoring to industrial applications to scientific research. An overview of the main ideas and developments in the field of ROVs is given in this abstract. These are remote-controlled, autonomous underwater vehicles that are operated by people on the surface. They are essential to deep-sea exploration because they let people go to places that would be dangerous or unreachable otherwise. With real-time data collection capabilities provided by ROVs that are outfitted with cameras, sensors, and manipulation tools, scientists can study marine ecosystems, geology, and biodiversity with previously unheard-of precision. Robotic underwater vehicles (ROVs) are utilized in industrial settings to perform tasks like underwater inspections, offshore structure maintenance, and underwater cable and pipeline installation. They are indispensable tools in situations where human intervention is unsafe or impractical due to their dexterity and adaptability.

articleTitle: Design and Development of Triple Energy Storage System (TESS) for Electric Vehicle Application
publicationTitle: 2024 Second International Conference on Smart Technologies for Power and Renewable Energy (SPECon)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel design and development of a Triple energy storage system(TESS) that combines lead acid and lithium ferro phosphate batteries with a capacitor bank for Electric Vehicle applications. The increase in electric vehicles needs to be supported by the existence of reliable energy storage devices. The battery, as an energy storage system, has its advantages and disadvantages. The combination of different battery types is chosen since the battery is one of the energy storage systems with mature technology and low life cycle cost. A solution that can be proposed to cover the weakness of each battery is the use of the combination different energy storage systems. Previously, a combination of Lithium ferro phosphate and lead acid batteries was used to solve this scenario. However, adding a capacitor bank can improve the results due to its rapid charge and discharge characteristics. In this paper, a battery control system with a combination of Valve Regulated Lead Acid (VRLA), Lithium Ferro Phosphate (LFP) batteries with capacitor bank was developed using the switching method. Battery selection switching is determined by the specification and operational set point of the battery, capacitor used.

articleTitle: Designing of MPPT Solar charge controller
publicationTitle: 2024 Second International Conference on Smart Technologies for Power and Renewable Energy (SPECon)
abstract: As the world transitions towards a more sustainable future, harnessing solar energy has emerged as a crucial avenue for reducing our reliance on traditional power sources. This paper explores the benefits of solar chargers coupled with maximum power point Tracking (MPPT) solar charge controllers, highlighting their combined potential to optimize energy conversion and storage.This paper presents the design and implementation of a maximum power point tracking (MPPT) solar charge controller utilizing a PIC micro-controller. The perturb and observe (P and O) algorithm MPPT technology is employed to address the inefficiency arising from the higher voltage produced by most solar panels compared to what is required for charging a 12 V battery. Typically, a 12 V charging panel generates a 16 to 18 Volt output, but only around 14.6 Volts is needed to charge most 12 V batteries, resulting in significant voltage wastage. The application of MPPT charging technology aims to convert this excess voltage into current, thereby enhancing overall charging efficiency in tandem with solar chargers.

articleTitle: Microgrid solutions for sustainable railway networks
publicationTitle: 2024 Second International Conference on Smart Technologies for Power and Renewable Energy (SPECon)
abstract: The recent railway system has evolved into an extensive microgrid, constituting a complex framework along distributed active loads, origin and storage devices. In this context, the active load is embodied by the trains, while the sources encompass a microgrid reliant on renewable energies. A prevalent challenge faced by many electrical trains is the inability to recuperate energy during regenerative braking phases, coupled with extended charging times at stations. This paper proposes a techno-economic approach to address these challenges by introducing supercapacitors (SCs) for energy storage within the trains, aimed at reducing overall energy consumption. The designed railway station incorporates photovoltaic (PV) and fuel cell sources, along with batteries forming an energy storage system (ESS). SCs play a crucial role in the train’s ESS, receiving power during braking phases and station stops through a pantograph integrated into an aerial power line. Supercapacitors are chosen for their high power characteristics, a substantial number of charge/discharge cycles, low specific energy and rapid charging capabilities. A power administration strategy is recommended to regulate the DC bus through voltage control and the buck-boost converter through current control. The sizing of the proportional-integral (PI) controller, essential for stabilizing the DC bus of both the train and station, is outlined. Design arrangement is meticulously modelled using MATLAB-Simulink.

articleTitle: Hybrid Fuzzy-Neuro System for Electrical Load Forecasting
publicationTitle: 2024 Second International Conference on Smart Technologies for Power and Renewable Energy (SPECon)
abstract: The adaptability of the CANFIS architecture to diverse data patterns and complexities is facilitated by the application of Bell and Gaussian functions. These membership functions play a crucial role in enabling the model to accurately capture the inherent uncertainties and nonlinearities present in real-world datasets. The utilization of the Delta Bar Delta algorithm for weight adaptation further enhances the model’s capacity to refine its parameters based on input data, contributing to improved accuracy in load prediction tasks. Additionally, the integration of Momentum learning mechanisms accelerates the learning process and fosters faster convergence, thereby enhancing the overall efficiency of the model. This paper delves into a thorough examination of how different configurations within the CANFIS framework influence key performance metrics such as prediction accuracy, generalization capacity, and learning efficiency. Through extensive experimentation conducted using datasets specifically tailored for load prediction, we aim to elucidate the nuanced effects of varying configurations on the model’s performance characteristics. By systematically analyzing the outcomes of these experiments, valuable insights can be gleaned to guide the selection of optimal configurations for practical implementation in real-world load forecasting scenarios.

articleTitle: An Image Processing Based Approach Towards Recognition of Underground Cable Defects
publicationTitle: 2024 Second International Conference on Smart Technologies for Power and Renewable Energy (SPECon)
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach for detecting possible faults in underground cables at the manufacturing industry using image processing techniques. With the increasing adoption of underground cables to minimize faults and outages in power transmission systems, ensuring the quality of these cables becomes crucial. Detecting defects at the manufacturing stage can save significant costs and effort by identifying faulty cables before they are deployed in the field. We propose a system that utilizes image processing algorithms to analyze cable images and identify potential faults, such as unbalanced currents, cable sheath faults, and short circuits. The system also calculates the area of each core to ensure equal current flow, and estimates the total cross-sectional area of the cable to assess the adequacy of insulation. The proposed approach offers a non-destructive and efficient method to enhance quality control in the manufacturing process of underground cables.

articleTitle: RC4 Cipher Based Securing of Data Exchange in Smart Grid
publicationTitle: 2024 Second International Conference on Smart Technologies for Power and Renewable Energy (SPECon)
abstract: A solution to the problems caused by data breaches in the production and distribution of power is provided by the smart grid framework’s inclusion of the RC4 Cipher algorithm. Individual entities can produce and sell electricity under the smart grid paradigm, which creates traffic in data management. To overcome these difficulties, the RC4 algorithm is suggested as a way to securely encrypt smart grid data. RC4 encryption is used during data exchange to guarantee the confidentiality and integrity of the data. According to the architecture, RC4 Cipher encryption is used to secure data on all connected nodes that make up the smart grid. While complete nodes at distribution points verify data and guarantee effective electricity routing, light nodes at the consumer level enable individual electricity generation and data handling of the energy supply, expedite transactions, and offer a secure foundation for handling the complexity of smart grid management. RC4 use in smart grids is a revolutionary way to increase electrical security, efficiency, and transparency. The goal of this integration is to improve the security.

articleTitle: Optimal Power Flow Using Improved Grey Wolf Optimization Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 Second International Conference on Smart Technologies for Power and Renewable Energy (SPECon)
abstract: This paper presents an Improved Grey Wolf Optimization (I-GWO) method for resolving the optimal power flow (OPF) issue. The I-GWO algorithm is proposed to improve population diversity, trade-off between exploration and exploitation, and also to avoid early convergence problems. The IGWO employs a dimension learning-based hunting (DLH) search technique acquired from the natural hunting behavior of individual wolves. The DLH strategy enhances the search capability and preserves diversity. The considered objectives are minimizing total fuel cost, active power loss, and voltage variations. A penalty method is used to tackle different constraints of the OPF issue. The I-GWO and GWO algorithms have been examined on the IEEE 30 -bus power system, and the obtained results are compared with other algorithms as available in the literature. The obtained outcomes are contrasted with other algorithms to show the superiority and robustness of the I-GWO method to solve the OPF problem.

articleTitle: Enhancing Solar Photovoltaic Efficiency through Incremental Conductance Maximum Power Point Tracking Technique: A Comprehensive Investigation
publicationTitle: 2024 Second International Conference on Smart Technologies for Power and Renewable Energy (SPECon)
abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive approach aimed at enhancing the performance of solar photovoltaic panels under varying sunlight conditions. The primary objective is to assess the operational dynamics of solar photovoltaic (PV) panels by scrutinizing the fluctuations in output power, current and voltage under different irradiation dynamics. An in-depth investigation into the performance of Incremental Conductance method Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT) technique has been performed. The analysis investigates the behavior of solar panel with MPPT and Boost converter under dynamic solar irradiation condition. Existing Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT) algorithms often lack the precision required for optimizing power output in a given solar system. In this investigation, the effect of step size involved in calculating Maximum Power Point (MPP) on transient performance of MPPT technique has been observed. The transient behavior of output power, voltage and current has been captured and investigated to find a link between MPPT step size and transient performance using MATLAB/Simulink platform. The findings of this paper present valuable insights for advancing the design and operation of solar photovoltaic systems in practical applications.

articleTitle: Static Load Modelling of Electric Vehicle Fast Charger For System Studies
publicationTitle: 2024 Second International Conference on Smart Technologies for Power and Renewable Energy (SPECon)
abstract: The Electric Vehicle has emerged as the most viable replacement to fossil fuel-powered automobiles. As a result, electric car load has emerged as a new source of load for power networks. The creation of charging infrastructure for electric vehicles is turning into an intriguing task for experts all over worldwide, and EV users should also have access to convenient and dependable charging facilities. Hence EV Fast charger model is developed and its efficacy on the system is studied using MATLAB simulations. The EV fast charging model is expressed as ZIP and Exponential static load using curve fitting application and it is seen that they profoundly behave as Constant Power Demand. Their impact on the stability of the power system is also explored.

articleTitle: Distributed Adaptive Virtual Impedance Control for Power Sharing in an Islanded Microgrid.
publicationTitle: 2024 Second International Conference on Smart Technologies for Power and Renewable Energy (SPECon)
abstract: Accurate active and reactive power sharing in islanded microgrids is a prominent challenge. The existing conventional droop control strategies for power-sharing have disadvantages like inaccurate power-sharing among distributed generators (DGs) in the case of feeder impedance mismatch, unequal ratings of the sources etc. The complexity intensifies in the case of reactive power sharing. Virtual impedance emerges as a widely adopted technique to address impedance mismatches; however, the key challenge lies in determining the optimal value for its configuration. This paper proposes an adaptive virtual output impedance-based control for proportionate sharing of powers among the parallel connected DGs in the microgrid. The proposed control method is evaluated with the information of neighbouring DGs with data integrity. The primary focus of the paper is to attain accurate reactive power sharing. A small signal stability analysis of the system is carried out to ensure its performance. Various case studies are simulated in MATLAB Simulink to validate the robustness of the proposed control strategy.

articleTitle: Single-Stage Bidirectional Three-Level AC/DC LLC Resonant Converter with High Power Factor
publicationTitle: 2024 Second International Conference on Smart Technologies for Power and Renewable Energy (SPECon)
abstract: The increasing demand for efficient and high-performance power converters in electric vehicle technology and renewable energy integration has brought attention to LLC resonant converters due to their advantages in soft switching, inherent short circuit and open circuit protection, and high efficiency. These converters are particularly well-suited for high-frequency operation, making them ideal for electric vehicle battery charging and other power conversion tasks. However, when integrated with a front-end boost power factor correction (PFC) stage in AC-DC applications, challenges arise in maintaining power balance during transients, leading to voltage fluctuations and potential operational instability. Moreover, light load conditions can result in excessive switching frequencies, causing elevated switching losses and control difficulties. Additionally, traditional LLC resonant converters face limitations related to high voltage stress on switches, which affects device reliability and overall converter performance. To address these issues, researchers have explored the use of multilevel inverters, but they introduce complexity and cost. In this context, this paper proposes a novel single-stage, three-level bidirectional AC-DC LLC-based resonant converter with features like zero voltage switching and duty ratio control for output voltage regulation. The converter achieves a unity displacement power factor naturally through discontinuous conduction mode. Simulation results demonstrate the converter’s effectiveness of the proposed topology. The proposed converter offers a promising solution for Electric vehicle chargers, combining unity power factor operation and efficient bidirectional power flow control in a single topology.

articleTitle: Analyzing the Performance of a Symmetrical Fifteen-Level Inverter with Component Reduction
publicationTitle: 2024 Second International Conference on Smart Technologies for Power and Renewable Energy (SPECon)
abstract: This study introduces a novel topology for a 15-level multilevel inverter with the objective of generating a more sinusoidal output voltage while utilizing a reduced number of power-consuming components. In the context of the growing prevalence of renewable energy systems, reliable and efficient power conversion methods are crucial for seamless integration and optimal performance. Multilevel inverters, in comparison to traditional two-level inverters, offer superior power quality, reduced harmonic distortion, and lower voltage stress on power equipment. The proposed topology, employing nine switches and eight DC voltage sources, aims to achieve 15 levels across the load with lower total harmonic distortion (THD). The design incorporates a Phase Disposition Pulse Width Modulation (PDPWM) control technique. Despite the reduced number of switches, this topology demonstrates advantages in achieving higher levels of output voltage.

articleTitle: Fault Detection Method for Inverter Interfaced Distributed Generators Based Microgrid
publicationTitle: 2024 Second International Conference on Smart Technologies for Power and Renewable Energy (SPECon)

authors.preferredName: Gubbala S S N S Manikanta

abstract: A microgrid is a small power distribution system consisting of a cluster of low-power generation units (micro energy sources) capable of operating independently, loads, energy storage, and energy conversion devices with associated protection and control units. Unlike traditional microgrids, the micro sources in all microgrids are inverter-interfaced distributed generators (IIDGs), in which the fault currents are 1.2-2 times the rated current. To ensure the stable operation of the microgrid requires to detect the faults within the minimum possible time. The data collected from Waveform Measurement Units (WMUs) are widely used to detect disturbances. When an event occurs, WMUs provide GPS-synchronized measurements of voltage and current waveforms in the time domain captured during the event. Given such data, a Lissajous curve can be developed, which is a graph constructed by plotting one waveform versus another. By utilizing this phenomenon, a new algorithm has been developed to detect and locate faults within the microgrid.

articleTitle: Solar Energy Driven and Multiple Sensor Based Smart Wheelchair for Enhanced Mobility of Physically Handicapped Individuals
publicationTitle: 2024 Second International Conference on Smart Technologies for Power and Renewable Energy (SPECon)
abstract: Automation is the use of advanced technologies without human intervention for operating equipment in desired manner. The paper describes this automation in its own unique way using a wheelchair, to make a smart and automated wheelchair that can be used by any aged person or physically impaired people. Smart wheelchair is an automated device designed to reduce human administration and force the wheelchair to follow the assigned instructions strictly. The wheelchair comprise of a joystick with the control of which an impaired person can move easily, it is also provided with obstacle avoider and edge detection that is given to the wheelchair to protect the person from any accident. The smart wheelchair is charged by solar panels, which provides a sustainable and ecofriendly solution to the power requirements of the smart wheelchair. Moreover, solar charging feature offers a cost-effective and durable energy solution. The wheelchair assists the disabled to move conveniently, while keeping cost at bay and affordable quality.

articleTitle: Intelligent Distribution Systems and Grid Integration of Renewable Energy Resources
publicationTitle: 2024 Second International Conference on Smart Technologies for Power and Renewable Energy (SPECon)
abstract: In the upcoming years, smart distribution systems will efficiently manage electricity supplied from varied sources, including solar and wind. This guarantees a dependable and smooth integration for both business and residential buildings. This abstract explores the power flow regulation and grid synchronization difficulties faced by Smart Distribution Systems (SDS). The system actively monitors dispersed energy supplies to ensure stability through the use of Advanced Control and Monitoring and Digital Signal Processor (DSP) programming. Connection of renewable energy sources (RES) and power system configuration synchronization are made possible by the use of Controller Area Network (CANBUS), a customized connection that resembles a parallel port. In order to facilitate remote monitoring, the system has an Ethernet port and GSM communication. Furthermore, a viable harmonic mitigation strategy is put forth that successfully lowers the levels of Total Harmonic Distortion (THD) during the conversion of DC to AC in the integration of renewable energy sources. This helps to promote the use of renewable energy in the future.

articleTitle: Analysis of Hybrid Distributed Generation System Using HOMER
publicationTitle: 2024 Second International Conference on Smart Technologies for Power and Renewable Energy (SPECon)
abstract: The Distributed Generation System is an emerging solution for fulfilling the power demand in remote rural areas. Distributed Generation (DG) is capable of providing reliable power at the site and no need for any transmission infrastructure. The efficiency of such a system can be improved with the aid of multiple technologies for generation. HOMER is a very useful software tool for technical and economic analysis of hybrid energy systems. In this paper hybrid system comprised of 3 sources solar, wind, and diesel generators is analyzed with the HOMER software.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of SyRM for EV Transportation Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 Second International Conference on Smart Technologies for Power and Renewable Energy (SPECon)
abstract: This paper models and investigates a variety of variable reluctance electric engines used in traction applications. Finding an optimal motor with the best qualities is the article’s primary goal. Synchronous Reluctance Motors (SynRM) are the motors under consideration for analysis. To figure out the behavior of the motor, the motors are analyzed in one, two, three, and four layers in angled barriers, notch and angled barriers, round barriers, notch and round barriers are evaluated in relation to parameters like torque ripple as well as average torque. The motors under consideration for analysis have the subsequent needs to have 2.5kW, 48 V, 20A, 1500 RPM, three phase. The motorsolve package is used to carry out the analysis in the finite element analysis environment.

articleTitle: Dynamic Economic Load Dispatch for a Campus Based on Renewable Energy Using HOMER
publicationTitle: 2024 Second International Conference on Smart Technologies for Power and Renewable Energy (SPECon)
abstract: Using examples from a school in Bhimavaram, India, this study discusses the economic and dynamic load dispatch at that institution. Since the institution is open during the day, load variances are primarily examined during that period. The load is assumed to be commercial and fed from an 11KV line. This improvement includes a two-way flow of energy from the institution to the grid and back again. run on 100 kW of solar panels, 95 kW of wind turbine, and 100 kWh of Li ion batteries. In order to maximize the utilization of renewable energy sources as well as minimize the need for generators that rely on fossil fuels, the best power utilization is supplied. The HOMER software is utilized for simulation in order to optimize a predetermined projected system.

articleTitle: Intelligent Battery Management System Integrated with Solar PV for Residential Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 Second International Conference on Smart Technologies for Power and Renewable Energy (SPECon)
abstract: The imperative to mitigate environmental harm is propelling the swift integration of renewable energy sources into the power grid. The intermittent generation of renewable energy can influence unpredictable electricity consumption, which can have security and system operation implications. To mitigate power generation fluctuations resulting from external factors such as wind speed, solar radiation, and climate variations, the implementation of a storage system becomes essential. The intelligence battery management system is crucial for contemporary battery- operated devices like electric automobiles, portable electronic devices, and renewable energy storage. It also enhances the battery’s lifespan, condition, and efficiency. Monitoring the battery’s state of charge is a critical aspect of battery management systems. This work focuses on monitoring the battery’s state of charge, temperature, and current for a solar panel system integrated with a battery for residential use. A microcontroller is utilized for control, while analog sensors are employed for detecting voltage and current parameters. Additionally, the research work emphasizes the design of an adaptive IoT communication protocol for efficient data transfer between the battery management system and Thing Speak, optimizing energy usage in IoT environments.

articleTitle: Analysis on effects of mountain shadow on solar energy capacity at western slope of Gangtok city using Shadowmap 3D-GIS mapping tool
publicationTitle: 2024 Second International Conference on Smart Technologies for Power and Renewable Energy (SPECon)
abstract: The research examines the influence of mountain shadow on the ability to generate solar electricity in the western slope of Gangtok, the capital city of state of Sikkim. An extensive study was conducted to examine the mean daily solar power insolation for a whole year, considering shadow effect from mountains. The study was carried out using a 3D GIS (Geographic Information System) mapping tool called the Shadowmap program. Solar radiation data was gathered to assess the amount of effective insolation received by the region, taking into account both direct and diffused sunshine. The study also evaluated the weekly fluctuations in altitude and azimuth angles experienced in the region. The study indicated an average energy loss of 21 percent due to the mountain shading effect. The effective altitude and azimuth angles range likewise was reduced by 15 and 10 percent, respectively compared to ideal calculation.

articleTitle: West Africa Power Pool Transmission Line Monitoring Using the Scada System
publicationTitle: 2024 Second International Conference on Smart Technologies for Power and Renewable Energy (SPECon)
abstract: The SCADA systems introduced in this study monitor the entire length of a 225 kV transmission line at 1,304 km for power disturbances caused by physical contact with conductors, which may distort the power flow. This novel approach to long transmission lines in this study has led to significant changes in the power systems in the region. Furthermore, the significance of this study on the West African Power Pool, especially for the CLSG transmission line of 225 kV in Sierra Leone and other countries served by the CLSG transmission line, is that it is impactful and has considerably improved electricity accessibility and availability in the region. Furthermore, rural electrification has substantially increased by connecting 99 towns and villages, and additional communities will be connected in the future by shield wires with 225 kV, addressing the lack of access to electricity in these areas, which can be easily monitored by using the SCADA system. This development has led to a notable increase in socioeconomic activities due to the increased energy availability in these areas. A SCADA has a better data management system, managing ICSs for data acquisition, communication, information sharing, and processing across the entire span of the transmission line ($1,304 \mathrm{~km}$), including substations. This approach enables the isolation of faulty areas through SCADA systems, unlike its counterpart, DCS, which is limited. The implemented SCADA for the CLSG transmission line in this study operates in frequency mode for power stabilization.

articleTitle: Fault Detection and Classification in PY Systems using MRA DWT and AdaBoost classifier
publicationTitle: 2024 Second International Conference on Smart Technologies for Power and Renewable Energy (SPECon)
abstract: The increasing integration of photovoltaic (PV) systems into the global energy grid emphasizes the need for robust fault detection and classification methodologies to ensure optimal performance and reliability. This research presents a novel approach for fault identification in PV arrays by combining the Multiresolution Analysis (MRA), Discrete Wavelet Transform (DWT), and AdaBoost classifier. The proposed methodology involves capturing the unique frequency and time-domain characteristics associated with various fault types within PV arrays. MRA is employed to extract relevant features from the acquired data, followed by DWT to enhance the discriminative power of the features. The processed data is then fed into an AdaBoost classifier, leveraging its ensemble learning capabilities to improve fault classification accuracy. Simulation and Experimental validation is conducted using real-world 3X3 PV array data under different fault scenarios, including shading, module failures, and electrical anomalies. The results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach in accurately detecting and classifying faults, even in the presence of noise and changing environmental conditions. Comparative analyses with existing fault detection methods highlight the superiority of the proposed MRA-DWT-AdaBoost framework in terms of accuracy, robustness, and computational efficiency.

articleTitle: An Integrated Method For High Current Detection In Sensorless Solar-Powered Brushless DC Water Pump, Eliminating Hall And Current Sensors
publicationTitle: 2024 Second International Conference on Smart Technologies for Power and Renewable Energy (SPECon)
abstract: A approach based on the back electromotive force (back-EMF) zero crossing is recommended for sensorless BLDC motor operation. The back-EMF is produced by the variation in line voltages. Neutral potential is therefore no longer required. Moreover, the recommended drive does not make advantage of phase current sensors. The speed is adjusted automatically depending on the available peak power of the PV array. The fundamental frequency is used to switch the parts of the voltage source inverter that power the BLDC motor pump. Switching losses are thereby decreased. Typical DC and AC motors are being gradually replaced with permanent magnet brushless DC motors because of their small size, high energy density, quiet operation, ease of control, maintenance-free operation, and high efficiency. Because of the development of power electronics and the availability of high-speed processors, brushless motor application fields are expanding daily. The creation of precise commutation to start the BLDC motor in position control is the hardest endeavor. For pumping water fed by photovoltaic arrays, a brushless motor is highly common. In order for a brushless motor to rotate in the appropriate direction, its position of the rotor must be used to drive a 3-phase VSI as electronic switch. Consequently, it is preferable to control of brushless motor, in order to raise the reliability, acceptability, and lower the cost and volume of brushless motors. This initialization technique primarily regulates the peak staring current and the precise starting commutation. The investigation of a setting up of the system for irrigation pump is also being conducted, as part of an ongoing effort to eliminate DC-DC converters. Design of the system is utilized to simulate all of these mentioned setups.

articleTitle: A Comprehensive Review on Exploring Drive Cycle Pattern Across Diverse Vehicle Load
publicationTitle: 2024 Second International Conference on Smart Technologies for Power and Renewable Energy (SPECon)
abstract: Investigating the complex interaction between static and dynamic elements, this study reveals how different loads and difficult terrains impact the patterns of drive cycles in vehicles. By tackling challenges faced during uphill climbs and downhill descents, the research contributes to a comprehensive comprehension of the various factors influencing vehicle performance. Through a detailed analysis of subtle dynamics, it offers valuable perspectives on the connections between drive cycle intricacies and diverse conditions, enhancing our understanding of vehicle behavior across different situations. The overarching goal of this thorough exploration is to make a substantial contribution to the field, pushing the boundaries of our knowledge regarding the intricate dynamics that govern vehicle performance and efficiency in a variety of conditions.

articleTitle: Short-term load forecasting using Artificial Bee Colony Optimization with Deep Learning Model on Power Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 Second International Conference on Smart Technologies for Power and Renewable Energy (SPECon)
abstract: In power systems, Short-term load prediction is a serious element of effective energy management as well as grid operation. It contains forecast of power demand over a quite short time prospect that ranges from hours to few days in advance. Exact load forecasting is vital for guaranteeing a steady and trustworthy power supply, enhancing generation and distribution, as well as allowing utilities to create knowledgeable choices about resource allocation and demand response plans. Leveraging historical information, climate situations, time of day, and other pertinent factors, advanced machine learning (ML) techniques used in order to offer exact load forecasts, assist grid operators in justifying imbalances, decrease operational costs, as well as improving general grid reliability. Therefore, this study presents a Short-term load forecasting using Artificial Bee Colony Optimization with Deep Learning (STLF-ABCDL) model on Power Systems. The STLF-ABCDL technique incorporates a multiple-stage procedure, starting with min-max normalization-based pre-processing for assuring data consistency. Besides, the STLF-ABCDL technique applies Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) for forecasting load. For boosting efficacy of LSTM model, the ABC algorithm can be utilized to tune the parameters and optimize network hyperparameters. The presented STLFABCDL technique exhibits considerable enhancements in the load prediction results, providing enhanced stability and optimal resource allocation.

articleTitle: Modified Convolutional Neural Network Algorithm for Categorization of Solar PV Panel Soiling
publicationTitle: 2024 Second International Conference on Smart Technologies for Power and Renewable Energy (SPECon)
abstract: The identification and categorization of soiling using artificial intelligence is essential for improving solar photovoltaic (PV) system efficiency. It is possible to use focused and effective cleaning techniques on solar panels by classifying and comprehending the particular types of pollutants. This research proposes a modified convolutional neural network (CNN) approach to efficiently classify soiling on solar PV panels. In contrast to the conventional method, the suggested CNN model is created using simple images rather than images plus time series data. As a result, processing speed is increased. Additionally, the suggested model achieved 96.91 percent accuracy. This success establishes our suggested methodology as a ground-breaking development in soiling type detection, providing improved accuracy and a unique strategy in contrast to current approaches. The trained and tested model is deployed on the web using the Flask. Flask is a powerful and flexible microweb framework for Python, Finally, a comparison is made between the existing method and the proposed method.

articleTitle: Cost-Effective Solutions for Underwater Ultrasonic Flow Rate Sensors in Renewable Energy Applications - an Appraisal
publicationTitle: 2024 Second International Conference on Smart Technologies for Power and Renewable Energy (SPECon)
abstract: Precise measurement of underwater fluid flow rates plays a critical role in diverse applications within the realm of smart technologies for power and renewable energy (PRE), including monitoring tidal energy infrastructure, optimizing hydropower generation, and safeguarding sensitive marine ecosystems. However, the high cost of traditional ultrasonic flow rate sensors hinders their widespread adoption in these applications. This paper critically analyzes recent advancements in underwater ultrasonic flow rate sensors, emphasizing novel cost-effective strategies and approaches specifically tailored for PRE applications. The paper classifies sensors based on their operating principles (transit-time, Doppler, and correlation) and delves into fundamental concepts, practical considerations, and recent developments. Notably, it identifies key challenges like material costs, transducer design complexity, and signal processing inefficiencies, ultimately limiting cost-effectiveness. The paper then explores potential solutions such as utilizing cheaper materials, employing innovative transducer designs, and implementing efficient signal processing techniques to address these challenges. Furthermore, the paper delves into ongoing research efforts and future directions aimed at further optimizing sensor performance and cost-efficiency for broader adoption within the dynamic field of smart power and renewable energy.

articleTitle: An Integrated Vehicle-To-Grid And Solar System For Energy Management And Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 Second International Conference on Smart Technologies for Power and Renewable Energy (SPECon)
abstract: In light of the high volatility of renewable energy sources, interconnecting them directly to the grid has the potential to cause substantial disruptions to the grid. When connected to the grid, energy storage systems such as electric vehicles (EVs) have the ability to employ flexible power consumption timing, controllable power usage, predictable power consumption, and intelligent power consumption habits. These characteristics can be utilized for grid energy management. The purpose of this study is to discuss the application of vehicle-to-grid technology for the purpose of energy management in order to reduce the variability of renewable energy systems such as solar and wind energy systems. Through the utilization of the vehicle to grid technology, plug-in electric vehicles (PEVs) and the batteries that power them are able to contribute to the maintenance and maintenance of the grid. The control solutions make it possible for the batteries of electric vehicles to contribute to the reduction of variations caused by solar photovoltaic power and to increase grid dependability by increasing the capacity to support peak demands. When compared to more conventional approaches, the simulation reveals that the implementation of an energy management and optimization technique for vehicle-to-grid systems results in significant improvements in performance.

articleTitle: Review on Microgrids, Control Strategies and DC Microgrids
publicationTitle: 2024 Second International Conference on Smart Technologies for Power and Renewable Energy (SPECon)
abstract: Due to the utilization of sources of clean energy like solar and wind energy, distributed power generation is essential to the energy industry. If cut off from the main electrical grid, a microgrid is a local grid with control features that can function on its own. Microgrids can function as standalone units or as part of a grid connection. There are three classifications of microgrids: hybrid, AC and DC. The DC microgrid, which links numerous distributed generation units to the power system, is the main topic of this study. A succinct overview of microgrids and associated control schemes is provided in this work.

articleTitle: SWOT Analysis of Distribution System in India: A Transition from Passive to Active
publicationTitle: 2024 Second International Conference on Smart Technologies for Power and Renewable Energy (SPECon)
abstract: India’s power system has been transiting towards a more decentralized operation with the deregulation being main driving force behind it. Apart from this, the adoption of renewable energy sources, reduction in aggregate losses, and growing energy access are some of the other driving factors. To support this, a lot of transformations needed to be done in the distribution sector to enhance energy efficiency, and maintain network security. A wide variety of distributed generation (DG) sources are needed to be integrated. Integrating, DG units in the distribution systems requires in-depth planning apart from the implementation of communication, active energy management, real-time monitoring, and distribution system (DS) automation. The application will create a need to transition from a passive distribution system (PDS) into active distribution systems (ADS). With an objective to create a strategic planning framework for this transition, this research presents a SWOT analysis to evaluate and compare both ADS and PDS highlighting their strengths, weaknesses, opportunities, and threats to completely understand the present situation and future development needs of the distribution system for integration of the DG unit as well as the Renewable energy sources. This will help in evaluating the system’s internal and external competitive advantages of ADS over PDS at the same time prioritizing the opportunities that an ADS provides.

articleTitle: Renewable Energy Efficiency of Unmanned Aerial Vehicles Operating with Wireless Sensor Networks and Mobile Ad Hoc Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 Second International Conference on Smart Technologies for Power and Renewable Energy (SPECon)
abstract: The amalgamation of Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) into Wireless Sensor Networks (WSNs) and Mobile Ad Hoc Networks (MANETs) provides significant prospects to improve network capabilities. This study examines the energy renewable efficiency and performance of UAVs operating in WSNs and MANETs. The assessment considers a variety of elements that influence energy consumption, including the possibility of integrating renewable energy, energy management measures, and the impact on overall network performance. This seeks to provide insights into optimizing energy usage and improving the operating efficiency of UAVs in these dynamic network situations through extensive analysis and evaluation. A special emphasis is placed on the management of mobility, the optimization of energy usage, and the effectiveness of routing protocols. The paper explores existing protocols such as LEACH, AODV and OLSR highlighting their benefits and challenges for UAV’s. A comparative analysis evaluates adapted protocols based on metrics such as energy efficiency, latency, and reliability.

articleTitle: A Integrated Charging Hub for Grid-Connected Electric Vehicles Powered by Renewable Energy
publicationTitle: 2024 Second International Conference on Smart Technologies for Power and Renewable Energy (SPECon)
abstract: In this paper, the charging dynamics of one or more electric car batteries connected to a traditional three-phase grid through a controlled rectifier and DC-DC converter. Two renewable energy sources that integrate seamlessly into the traditional grid are photovoltaic arrays (PVA) and wind farms. The battery charging procedure optimizes the energy derived from these sustainable sources. When there is insufficient renewable energy available, the rectifier uses the three-phase grid to produce electricity for battery charging. A comprehend control framework for energy management is simulated, encompassing the grid, residential loads, electric vehicle charging stations, and sustainable energy resources. Using MATLAB Simulink software, we analyze many operational scenarios while accounting for changing environmental factors that affect both renewable sources and EV battery charging. The ‘powergui’ toolbox is used to provide graphical representations of system performance over time under different conditions.

articleTitle: A Comprehensive Review on Opportunities and Challenges of Grid Integration of Renewable Energy Resources
publicationTitle: 2024 Second International Conference on Smart Technologies for Power and Renewable Energy (SPECon)
abstract: The global shift towards sustainable energy has accelerated the integration of Variable Renewable Energy Resources (VRER), such as solar and wind, into mainstream power generation. While VRER offer immense potential for reducing carbon emissions and advancing energy sustainability, their inherent variability poses unique challenges for seamless integration into existing power grids. This paper comprehensively explores challenges and opportunities associated with the efficient grid integration of VRER. A key focus of the paper is to maintain system stability and reliability while improving the economic benefits of incorporating VRER. By offering a balanced examination of challenges and opportunities, this paper aims to guide stakeholders in developing effective policies, technologies, and strategies for navigating the complex landscape of VRER grid integration. Ultimately, the insights presented contribute to realizing a sustainable and resilient future energy system.

articleTitle: Enhancing Efficiency and Improving Power Quality in Grid-Connected 17-Level Multilevel Inverters for Renewable Energy Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 Second International Conference on Smart Technologies for Power and Renewable Energy (SPECon)
abstract: This research paper underscores the critical importance of enhancing efficiency and refining power quality in grid-connected 17-level multilevel inverters (MLIs) utilized in renewable energy applications. With the escalating demand for sustainable energy sources, MLIs serve as pivotal components in efficiently converting and delivering power. The paper is dedicated to optimizing the performance of the 17-level MLI architecture, which is crucial for the grid integration of renewable sources. Through the implementation of advanced control strategies and innovative modulation techniques, the research endeavors to elevate the overall efficiency of the inverter system while simultaneously addressing concerns related to power quality. The investigation reveals a peak voltage total harmonic distortion (THD) of 324.51 Volts and an overall THD of 15.62%. The proposed models involve only 9 power switches, whereas the existing model necessitates 32. By effectively mitigating harmonic distortions and ensuring seamless power transfer, these proposed enhancements aim to significantly enhance the reliability and stability of grid- connected renewable energy systems. The findings offer a more robust and effective solution, facilitating the smooth integration of renewable energy into existing power grids.

articleTitle: Modelling an Electric Vehicle Smart Grid: Sustainability, Integration, and Optimisation
publicationTitle: 2024 Second International Conference on Smart Technologies for Power and Renewable Energy (SPECon)
abstract: Electric vehicles (EVs) are gaining substantial traction in the transportation industry, which is a crucial driver in the mobility revolution. Electric vehicles have sparked considerable interest around the world. However, because coal accounts for over two-thirds of India’s electricity generation, charging EVs with this energy only moves pollution from highways to other regions of the country where the power plant is located. To address these problems and maximize the potential of EVs within the context of current power infrastructure, an intelligent and efficient residential smart grid model must be developed. This study offers a dynamic and adaptive smart grid paradigm based on solar energy, with the goal of accelerating the transition of EVs to an eco-friendly electric transportation future.This paper describes the proposed smart grid model’s architecture, operation, and practicality. It also provides a solid basis for developing an electric vehicle smart grid model to optimize EV charging, improve grid stability, and aid in sustainable energy management. The author’s smart grid model includes the installation of EV chargers, smart meters capable of remotely reading electricity use, remote service connection and disconnection, and the delivery of electricity to neighbouring homes that require the service. The potential benefits of this proposed smart grid approach in steering the transition to sustainable and electric transportation are thoroughly studied. The model’s validation includes an examination of energy consumption patterns among various user segments, as well as an investigation of customers’ proclivity to adopt solar systems. Following the collection of data on the capital and maintenance costs of solar systems from various vendors, an evaluation of the costs associated with the proposed smart grid model is carried out, supported by a full mathematical analysis, including breakeven considerations. The findings show that the smart grid model can effectively function as a sustainable mechanism for charging vehicles and supplying residential electricity.

articleTitle: Comparative Evaluation of 6T, 8T and 10T Ternary SRAM Cells Schemes for Future VLSI and Power Electronics
publicationTitle: 2024 Second International Conference on Smart Technologies for Power and Renewable Energy (SPECon)
abstract: A ternary SRAM cell can be built as a restorage element by joining ternary inverters back-to-back. In this work, it is shown that the evaluation of ternary logic using the 8 T SRAM cell is superior than that using the 10T SRAM cell. SRAM cells with 10T and 8 T capacities are used to test the many designs. With its tiny space and power efficiency, the 8 T ternary SRAM cell is becoming a top contender for next-generation on-chip memories as VLSI technology keeps becoming smaller. The 8T architecture allows for the dependable storing of three logic states per cell due to the extra transistors compared to a regular 6T SRAM cell. With ternary storage, one can keep noise margins the same while increasing memory density. Ternary 8T SRAM is an ideal candidate for more research and optimization as a small, energy-efficient memory subsystem because to its dependable performance and simple control logic.

articleTitle: Review on Intelligent Social Networking Algorithms and Their Effects on Predicting the Adequacy of Renewable Energy Sources via Social Media
publicationTitle: 2024 Second International Conference on Smart Technologies for Power and Renewable Energy (SPECon)
abstract: With millions of people tuning into social media platforms, tech giants have turned their users into datacenters. Almost no attention is given to how the underlying algorithms of software and applications on users’ screens try to manipulate their thoughts and actions. Since people spend so much of their time glued to their screens, it is crucial to analyze social media algorithms to understand their impact on one’s life. Some people even use these platforms to scale businesses by increasing user demands. This article aims at understanding the overview of different social networking algorithms and learn the numerous techniques used to gain profits.
